The ex vivo susceptibility of P. falarum isolates to the drugs Dihydroartemisinin (the active metabolite of artemether) and Lumefantrine, two drugs of the ACT, was unchanged in Senegal.
the prevalence of Plasmodum falciparum with reduced susceptibility has not decreased in Dakar, but has increased for mefloquine and doxycylcine.

In summary, our research is concerned with

the study of the in vitro sensitivity of Plasmodiun falciparum isolated in Senegal to the main antimalarial molecules in use in Senegal, in order to assess the risk of the emergence of drug resistance.
the ex vivo susceptibility to anti-malaria drugs of Plasmodia falciparum strains isolated from patients treated in the Dakar area.
the ex vivo susceptibility to anti-malaria drugs of Plasmodum falciparum strains collected in Dakar, Senegalese, between 2012 and 2014.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the ex vivo susceptibility to the anti-malarial agents tested has not changed in the last 10 years.

, in the Dakar area, the introduction of ACT in the treatment of P. falarum infections did not result in an increased prevalence of in vitro resistant isolations, but it did result in an increased proportion of in vitro resistant P. falciparuim isolations.
the in vitro resistance of P. faldiparum isolates to anti-malarials in Senegal remains low.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the ex-vivo susceptibility of Plasmonium falciparium to anti-malarials in Senegal was assessed at the Military Hospital of Dakar, Senegalese.
the introduction of ACT in Senegal has not induced a reduction in P. faliiparum susceptibility to anti-malaria drugs.
the ex vivo susceptibility to the drugs of P. faldiparum in Dakar is not affected by the widespread introduction of ACT.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the introduction of ACT in the country has not induced an increase in parasite resistance to the drugs Dihydroartemisinin (a common ACT component) and Lumefantrine.
there has been a significant increase in the prevalence of P falciparum parasites with reduced susceptibility to MQ and DOX, which are both common ACT partner drugs.
the ex vivo susceptibility to anti-malaria drugs is a reliable tool that should be used in combination with molecular markers of resistance to assess the efficacy of malaria treatment.
